name: 100X.VC
identity_check: 100X.VC (also written 100X VC) at 100x.vc: Mumbai-based early-stage venture fund launched in July 2019 and led by Sanjay Mehta, the first Indian VC to invest through iSAFE notes. ET calls it a SEBI-registered Category I AIF backed by Mehta Ventures (Mehta's family office). Confirmed by domain, the site's own description and team page, and ET, Inc42, YourStory and Entrepreneur India coverage. Not 100IN (100in.vc), a 2026 Brussels pre-seed firm that startupintros.com mixes up with 100X.VC. Not Mehta Ventures itself (the sponsor), and not Pidilite Ventures (a corporate VC it sources deals for).

thesis_text.value: Mumbai micro-VC (SEBI Category I AIF backed by Sanjay Mehta's family office) writing first institutional cheques of ₹1.25 Cr to early-stage Indian startups through iSAFE notes: an India SAFE structured as CCPS, with cap, discount or MFN variants; in 2022 it was weighing about 15% future equity per cheque. Sector-agnostic; invests in cohorts ('Classes') ending in an investor pitch day.

open_items: Valuation cap and discount: no figure on any fetched page. The iSAFE page lists four template variants (valuation cap with discount, valuation cap, discount, MFN) as DocSend links, which were not opened (DocSend may ask for an email). The only equity marker is Inc42 (Apr 2022): 'mulling' 15% future equity for the cheque, with no cap stated.

application_url not found: the site (only 4 pages per its sitemap, Oct 2026) has no apply form, contact or email. Cohorts were drawn from open applications (1,900+ for Class 12; rolling applications with no deadlines in 2022). The current intake route is unknown.

US-flipped companies: iSAFE is a CCPS under Indian law, so the standard instrument needs an Indian company. No page says whether 100X.VC will invest in a Delaware parent. Inc42 Datalabs lists one portfolio company (Airbook) with HQ in San Francisco, a hint only.

No Class 13 or later cohort found. The homepage still shows 180 companies, the count reported after Class 12 (Jan 2025). The latest dated activity found is participation in Agnikul Cosmos (Nov 2025). The web-search quota ran out mid-task, so 2025–26 coverage was checked only through ET's 100X.VC topic page and known article URLs. A follow-up search for Class 13 or 2026 deals is worth doing.

Funds: only the INR 125 Cr fund (announced Apr 2022) was found, with no vehicle name or close date. SEBI Category I AIF status comes from ET (Jun 2024) and Inc42; the registration number is unconfirmed because the SEBI register query returned HTTP 530. The 2019 'over Rs 200 crore' (ET) was a target for a corporate-VC partner programme, not a fund. No Fund II found.

No stated AI or manufacturing focus. Manufacturing links: Class 12's Cellarim Labs, and a Sep 2022 partnership to source strategic deals for Pidilite Industries' venture arm (ET). Whether that partnership is still active in 2026 was not checked.
Company LinkedIn comes only from the Inc42 Datalabs profile (database). Partner LinkedIn profiles are not linked on 100x.vc, and partner focus sectors are not stated.

Class 12 rounds: stage not stated; the date is the cohort announcement (18–20 Jan 2025), not the closing date. Websites for Numberlabs, Selkea and Telescope are unconfirmed (numberlabs.ai refused the connection; selkea.ai showed only a title). The other company websites were confirmed on the listed company pages. Those pages are not attached to rounds because they do not mention 100X.VC.

Agnikul Cosmos: the '$500 million valuation' is not recorded as post-money because the article does not specify. The ET URL slug says Rs 150 crore while the text says $17 million. 100X.VC's share is undisclosed.
Breathe ESG (Nov 2023) is included to evidence that 100X.VC leads; ET gives no HQ or website for it.

Not followed up: Inc42 Datalabs hints that Cellarim Labs raised a second (seed) round in Dec 2025 and that Scoutflo's only round is dated Apr 2025. Accio Robotics (robotics) is in the portfolio per Inc42 Datalabs; no round article was fetched.

Class 11 (Jun 2024; 17 startups incl. Deepvue.tech, GoCodeo, EasyReplenish, Kroto per ET) not recorded as rounds: outside the 24-month window, and enough recent rounds were found. Other Class 12 companies (Currychief, Famyo, Gape Labs, NuMode, PiePay, Propall, Trado, WeTeach, Vantify) were skipped as consumer or unclear B2B fit.
